cues: The file is bone-marrow dot A R F F: one hundred eighty-seven children, and thirty-seven columns.

The clock is survival time, days from transplant, from six days out to three thousand three hundred sixty-four. The event is survival status. One means the child died. Zero means follow-up ended while they were still alive. That zero is censoring: we know they lived at least that long, and we do not know what happened after.
Eighty-five patients died. One hundred two were censored.

A reverse Kaplan–Meier, which treats censoring as the event, puts median follow-up at one thousand five hundred twenty-two days. Ordinary median survival is never reached, because more than half the cohort is still alive at the last follow-up.
